items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: I used to go up and see him, we used to go up and see him, we used to go and hang out for three days.

ctx.x: I worked days, too. I drove cabs and worked in a car battery factory and the whole thing. It’s just whatever comes up. I mean I’m a family man, I come from a very strong type family so that’s the way I felt. I mean if I couldn’t do it playing the trumpet I had to do something to keep some bread coming in you know. So I mean I’ve done a lot of things. And that’s why I decided to move to Vegas. I was making $82.50 a week in a car battery factory, and that’s 5-1/2 days a week. So I figured well, you know, I could…
I used to go up and see him, we used to go up and see him, we used to go and hang out for three days.
He had a big studio in his garage. He’d turn the tape on and we’d play all night. He must have tapes that —
